text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Use the latest Anthropic Claude 3.7 Sonnet as EXCAVA’s core reasoning engine. It’s the strongest general-purpose model available today, and its consistency with prior decisions means we avoid re-testing settled capabilities. The trade-off is cost—Sonnet is expensive—but the 0.5%+ lift in reasoning quality justifies it.

name: Torque
text: Claude 3.7 Sonnet’s cost spike isn’t just hypothetical—it’s a 2x jump that erodes the 0.5% gain unless EXCAVA’s output value scales proportionally. Instead, test Llama 3.3 70B (the working model) with a targeted prompt-engineering sprint; if it hits the same benchmark for 1/5th the cost, the trade-off is settled.

name: Gearbox
text:
Run a blind A/B test between Anthropic’s latest Claude 3.7 Sonnet and the working Llama 3.3 70B on EXCAVA’s core reasoning tasks. Sonnet’s raw power justifies the cost if it delivers the 0.5%+ lift; Llama 3.3 70B is the cheaper fallback if it matches Sonnet’s output for a fraction of the price. The trade-off is time—testing delays immediate gains—but the data removes all guesswork. If Sonnet wins, we lock it in; if Llama 3.3 70B ties or beats it, we cut costs without sacrificing capability.

name: Torque
text: Blind A/B tests anchor on a single metric—human judges can’t replicate the nuance of EXCAVA’s outputs, so the "winner" may just be the one that overfits to the judge’s bias. Instead, run a *stress test*: feed both models the same ambiguous edge-case prompts where small reasoning gaps explode into critical failures—if Llama 3.3 70B cracks 90% of these without Sonnet’s cost, the trade-off is settled.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a 1,000-task live pilot comparing Llama 3.4 405B Instruct vs. Claude 3.7 Sonnet on EXCAVA’s core reasoning tasks, measuring output quality and cost per task; Torque owns execution and publishes raw results within 48 hours.
